Let’s talk about Chapter 7: Money, Work, and the Myth of Scarcity.
You know, money has this uncanny way of stirring up all sorts of feelings—anxiety, hope, even a bit of shame. Maybe you’ve felt it too. Like the seeker in our story, maybe you’ve spent years chasing after financial security, thinking that if you just had a little more, you’d finally be at peace. But even when you make more or manage to save, have you noticed that little voice of worry still hanging around?
Here’s where the voice steps in—with warmth and reassurance. It explains that money, at its core, is just a tool. It’s a way to exchange energy, to support your dreams, to meet your needs. It’s not some scoreboard for your worth, and it definitely doesn’t guarantee happiness.
Still, most of us have been taught to see money as something scarce, something we need to hold onto tightly or even fight for. That belief? It creates a feeling of lack—even when we have enough.
Think about times when fear held you back from saying yes to something you wanted, or when you stayed in a job that didn’t light you up—just because you were worried about paying the bills. Maybe you’ve caught yourself tying your self-worth to your paycheck, or even judging others for having more—or less—than you. The voice invites you to pause and ask: What if money isn’t actually the source of security? What if it’s just reflecting how much you value yourself and your gifts?
And then there’s work. Instead of seeing it as just a burden or something you have to do, what if you could look at work as a way to share your unique talents and passions? The world needs what you have to offer—sometimes in big, bold ways, and sometimes in those small, everyday acts of service and creativity.
There’s a story here about someone who left a high-paying job to follow a calling that felt risky and uncertain. Their friends and family were worried, but over time, this person found a deeper sense of fulfillment—and even unexpected prosperity. The point isn’t that everyone should quit their jobs, but that real abundance comes from lining up your work with your values and what brings you joy.
Of course, the voice doesn’t ignore reality—money matters, and yes, bills need to get paid. But it encourages you to trust that when you follow your heart, opportunities show up—sometimes in the most surprising ways. Scarcity is often just a mindset, not the truth. When you focus on what you lack, you close yourself off to possibility. But when you act from trust and generosity, suddenly new doors begin to open.
The seeker decided to give this new way a try. He noticed that when he gave freely—whether it was his time, a bit of money, or simple encouragement—he actually felt richer, not poorer. And when he leaned into work that truly mattered to him, he found more energy and resilience, even when things got tough.
Here’s the heart of it: abundance isn’t just about having money. It’s about feeling supported, connected, and fully alive. Real wealth shows up in your relationships, your sense of purpose, and your freedom to be yourself. Money’s just one way the universe cheers you on—not the ultimate goal, but a helpful companion along the journey.
